definitions.explanation: A fence made of bamboo, characteristic of Japanese gardens, temple grounds, and traditional residences. Various styles exist (e.g., {四目垣|よつめがき} open lattice, {建仁寺垣|けんにんじがき} vertical screen).

examples.japanese: {庭|にわ}を{竹垣|たけがき}で{囲|かこ}んだ。
examples.english: I enclosed the garden with a bamboo fence.

examples.japanese: {寺|てら}の{周|まわ}りには{古|ふる}い{竹垣|たけがき}があった。
examples.english: There was an old bamboo fence around the temple.

examples.japanese: {京都|きょうと}の{町家|まちや}には、{細|ほそ}い{道|みち}に{沿|そ}って{低|ひく}い{竹垣|たけがき}が{続|つづ}いている。
examples.english: In Kyoto's traditional townhouses, low bamboo fences run along the narrow streets.

notes:
Compound of {竹|たけ} (bamboo) + {垣|かき} (fence; the kanji shifts to が as the second element). Bamboo fences are emblematic of Japanese garden design and come in many named styles.

COMMON STYLES:
- {四目垣|よつめがき}: open four-square lattice fence (common in tea gardens)
- {建仁寺垣|けんにんじがき}: vertical solid bamboo screen (named after Kennin-ji)
- {御簾垣|みすがき}: horizontal blind-style fence

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {竹垣|たけがき}を{囲|かこ}う: to enclose with a bamboo fence
- {竹垣|たけがき}を{結|ゆ}う: to construct (tie together) a bamboo fence
- {古|ふる}い{竹垣|たけがき}: an old bamboo fence
